title: Impact of sex on the efficacy of first-line Y90-Radioembolization plus/minus Sorafenib versus Sorafenib alone in Patients With BCLC B/C HCC – An exploratory, retrospective analysis of the Phase III SORAMIC/SARAH/SIRVENIB trials
summary: This study investigates whether gender has an influence on the success of treatment in patients with liver cancer (HCC). Existing data will be analyzed to find out whether men and women respond differently to certain treatments. Specifically, the aim is to examine whether gender influences the survival time and the course of the disease after drug therapy or a special form of radiotherapy (Y90 radioembolization).
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts

interventions.name: The data of the study population from the Phase II/III studies SORAMIC, SARAH and SIRVENIB form the basis for the retrospective analysis. Patients with intermediate or advanced stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) according to the BCLC (Barcelona for liver cancer) classification were included. Patie

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients treated within the SORAMIC, SARAH and SIRVENIB study
Exclusion criteria:
Missing information regarding gender
